summary: Lambda's Research Grant offers qualifying researchers up to $5,000 in credits for Lambda on-demand GPU Instances. The research hub (lambda.ai/research) hosts the apply-for-a-grant CTA and describes the program as research and mentorship; the $5,000 figure is stated on Lambda's CVPR 2026 page and ICLR 2026 blog, which point applicants back to lambda.ai/research. The ICLR post addresses independent researchers who need compute; the official pages reviewed do not require venture backing or state a card requirement. The linked application requires contact name/email, research problem, relevance/novelty, challenges, GPU compute needs, notable achievements, roadmap and publishing plan. Applicants must answer whether they are willing to co-write a Lambda blog; a required yes/no question is not evidence that yes is mandatory. Company, related publications and profile links are optional. No ORCID or institutional affiliation requirement was found in the current form.
claim_steps: Review the current grant CTA at https://lambda.ai/research and open its linked Research Grant application.
Prepare required first/last name, email, research problem, relevance and novelty, challenges, GPU compute needs, notable achievements, roadmap and publishing plan.

Answer the required yes/no question about willingness to co-write a Lambda blog. Company, related publications, GitHub/Scholar/social profiles and partnerships are optional; do not invent an ORCID or affiliation prerequisite.
Submit only your own accurate research application. If awarded, use the up-to-$5,000 credits on Lambda’s on-demand GPU Instances; exact award and expiry are not guaranteed by the public form.
